extracted.intended_audience: contemporaneous political correspondents (Madison, Jay, Adams) and readers interested in 18th-century diplomacy, commerce, and federal governance (historians, researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted normative statements and practical recommendations from Thomas Jefferson's 1787 correspondence about federal structure, diplomacy, commerce, consular protection, and administrative practice. The page is a set of letters addressed to political figures describing what Jefferson considers appropriate policy and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of executive business from Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea of separating the executive business of the confederacy from Congress, as the judiciary is already in some degree, is just and necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson favors creating that separation by a federal act rather than relying on an internal committee of Congress; he warns a committee acting during sessions would demand more self-denial than Congress likely possesses. (Context: he had proposed appointing an executive committee to act during sessions, but thinks a federal act is preferable.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to giving Congress a blanket negative over State acts
rubrics_metrics.description: The negative proposed to be given them on all the acts of the several legislatures, is now, for the first time, suggested to my mind. Prima facie, I do not like it. It fails in an essential character; that the hole and the patch should be commensurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson argues a blanket negative would give federal authority far more power than needed (cover the whole garment to mend a small hole). He warns it will create preliminary questions for nearly every state act and produce frequent debate about whether an act 'concerns the confederacy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer appeals to federal courts for conflicts between state law and Confederation/treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: Would not an appeal from the State judicature to a federal court, in all cases where the act of Confederation controlled the question, be as effectual a remedy, and exactly commensurate to the defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson gives the example of a British creditor suing in Virginia where a state act excludes him: appealing to a federal court (when Confederation/treaty controls) corrects state judges who might be 'weak' to local views. He notes the risk that a federal court may encroach on state jurisdiction but sees Congress as a check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urgency of selling western lands to pay public debt
rubrics_metrics.description: I am uneasy at seeing that the sale of our western lands is not yet commenced. That valuable fund for the immediate extinction of our debt will, I fear, be suffered to slip through our fingers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson warns delay exposes the fund to unpredictable events and risks separation of the western populations if not retained until their governments become settled and wise. Timely disposition is necessary to secure national finance and unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid high-risk diplomatic missions likely to fail and provoke public disappointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposition of my going to Madrid, to try to recover ... I should think desperate. ... the strong probability of failure and the public disappointment directed on me, in the other, the latter preponderates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He recommends weighing personal pleasure and bare possibility of success against the high probability of failure and resulting public disappointment; also warns such a move could excite jealousy that would make the mission worse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer foreign debts when strategically beneficial to avoid local political friction
rubrics_metrics.description: We should try to transfer this debt elsewhere, and leave nothing capable of exciting ill thoughts between us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson proposes moving debts (e.g., from France to Holland) to remove sources of public censure and protect credit, using available negotiators (Dumas, Adams) where skill and position make them better suited to the task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiate tariff and trade concessions proactively with host government
rubrics_metrics.description: I have had it much at heart to remove from between us every subject of misunderstanding or irritation. ... I am in hopes, in addition to those, to obtain a suppression of the duties on tar, pitch, and turpentine, and, an extension of the privileges of American whale oil, to their fish oils in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson outlines concrete commercial objectives (duty suppression, extension of privileges) and reports sustained solicitations to the Comptroller General and reliance on Arrêts and official letters to secure retrospective relief and refunds for duties already paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiply points of contact to strengthen bilateral relations and remove irritants
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides endeavoring, on all occasions, to multiply the points of contact and connection with this country, which I consider as our surest mainstay under every event, I have had it much at heart to remove from between us every subject of misunderstanding or irritation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical diplomacy should increase commercial and political connections while removing specific causes of friction (e.g., unpaid debts to officers and farmers) to sustain friendly relations and national interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consular rank does not guarantee immunity from local legal process for debt
rubrics_metrics.description: He observed, that the character of Consul is no protection in this country, against process for debt: that as to the character with which Mr. Barclay had been invested at the court of Morocco, it was questionable whether it would be placed on the diplomatic line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson reports that consular commissions may only protect within limited locales (e.g., Paris) and stresses the need for letters of safe conduct or creditor consent to secure travel and protection; advises pragmatic measures (consent of creditors, safe conduct letters) rather than assuming immunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local officials and legal remedies to secure citizens abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Barclay has probably informed you of his having been arrested in Bordeaux ... He immediately applied to the parliament of that place, who ordered his discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson documents using local Procureur General and Parliament to obtain release; he recommends thanking and cultivating favorable local officials and using the local legal/political system as the practical avenue for relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect port-level commercial intelligence to estimate trade importance
rubrics_metrics.description: I was desirous, while at the sea-ports, to obtain a list of the American vessels which have come to them since the peace, in order to estimate their comparative importance to us, as well as the general amount of our commerce with this country, so far as carried on in our own bottoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson sought concrete lists from Marseilles, Cette, Bayonne, Bordeaux, Nantes, and L'Orient; he notes the likely imperfections of such lists but treats them as necessary inputs for commercial policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote American exports by learning local consumer preferences and supply differences
rubrics_metrics.description: I found the difference to be, not in the management, as had been supposed ... but in the species of rice; and I hope to enable them in Carolina, to begin the cultivation of the Piedmont rice ... I satisfied myself of the practicability of introducing our whale-oil for their consumption...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson recommends empirical investigation (travel, sample comparisons) to identify product differences and adapt cultivation/marketing so American producers can supply both qualities demanded; engage local merchants to prepare markets rather than acting unilaterally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address administrative bottlenecks and hold contractors/workmen accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Stockdale ... printed his edition completely in three weeks. ... Barrois ... had kept [the plate] three months ... I wrote him word in return, to deliver the plate instantly. ... I would apply to the police.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson expects prompt performance from printers and workmen, will use pressure (messages, orders, police) if necessary, and prefers to assign work to diligent printers rather than tolerate habitual delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer practical small payments over asking repeated favors
rubrics_metrics.description: It being my opinion and practice to pay small sums of money, rather than to ask favors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When minor help is needed from foreign officials or servants, Jefferson prefers to pay modest sums to secure action rather than rely on repeated personal solicitations that could be inappropriate or ineffective.
